newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECHS CONDEMN BELGRADE VIOLENCE.
newsitem.headline: CZECHS CONDEMN BELGRADE VIOLENCE.

text.p: The Czech Republic on Monday condemed Sunday's police violence against pro-democracy demonstrators in Belgrade and called on Serbia to recognise opposition victories in municipal elections.

"(The Czech Foreign Ministry) condemns the brutality and disproportionate police interference, which does not lead to a resolution of the politcal crisis and further intensifies tensions in the country," the ministry said in a statement.

Serbian security police attacked thousands of peaceful demonstrators overnight, injuring more than 100 in the most violent clash of the 76 days of protests which followed the government's rejection of opposition electoral victories.

In a country where the Communist government was ousted more than seven years ago soon after a similar clash between police and student demonstrators, the now-democratic Czech Republic issued its strongest statement yet against the government of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.

"The means which the police used yesterday against protestors is disproprtionate to the character of the demonstrations and is evidence that the Serbian government is not considering to reconcile with the defeat which it suffered in municipal elections," the ministry said.

"(The Czech ministry) is of the opinion that immediate acknowledgement of the results of the November elections and a cessation of violence against demonstrators is the only way for Serbia to return to the community of democratic states."

Czech President Vaclav Havel, a long-time dissident who helped lead demonstrations which resulted in the fall of the Communist government less than a month after a major clash with students, has yet to comment on Sunday's violence in Belgrade.
